text:
maria: FYI we just got an urgent support ticket from ACME — p95 latency jumped ~40% in us-west after yesterday's runtime rollout (v2.7.4 -> v2.8.0). customer is hitting timeouts.

josh: ugh. is this the quant/scheduler change that went out yesterday?

maria: looks like it. deploy-bot shows config flag `enable_quant_fastpath=true` + scheduler update.

sasha: can you paste the chart? which endpoints/routes are worst?

maria: embedding/vec and generate/chat are both up. p50 fine, p95/p99 tail is the problem. stack: g4dn-like infra. here's the alert snippet:
```
p95_us_west/runtime_requests: 420ms -> 590ms (baseline 420ms)
p99_us_west/runtime_requests: 880ms -> 1200ms
error_rate: unchanged
samples: 1200/min
```

roland: interesting that error rate didn't change — points to slow-path bursts (cold kv cache or kernel slowdown). any cluster-level IO or CPU spikes?

maria: host metrics look normal, GPU util steady. CPU scheduler wait increased on the runtime side for a subset of hosts.

jeeves (infra-bot): Deployed runtime v2.8.0 -> 2026-03-16 03:12 UTC. Flags: enable_quant_fastpath, new_scheduler_v2.

sasha: let's bisect config first before rolling back full deploy. steps:
1) split traffic 90/10 to v2.7.4 and v2.8.0 for the affected route
2) compare p95 by tenant and kernel selector
3) toggle quant fastpath to false on a cohort and measure
4) if still bad, revert scheduler change on a small cohort

maria: on it. creating canary split now. support-bot, attaching ticket 87912 to this thread.

support-bot: Ticket #87912: ACME - high p95 latency (post-rollout). Customer reported timeouts at 10:22 PST.

josh: for reproducibility, can someone run a controlled synthetic workload against both versions? small seq len 256 and long seq 1024. prefer to repro locally on a canary host.

eva: I'll run synthetic workload on canary hosts and capture latency histograms + pprof flame. also will capture kvcache hit rates.

sasha: sample repro command (use test-api key, limited qps):
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
curl -s -X POST https://canary-us-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-13b","input":"repeat x 1024","max_tokens":512}' &
done
```

roland: capture traces with trace_id header so we can correlate across services. also enable the latency debug probes on the runtime process for 10m.

maria: split applied: 85% -> v2.8.0, 15% -> v2.7.4 for ACME route. metrics streaming in.

(10m later)

eva: repro results: v2.7.4 p95=430ms, v2.8.0 p95=610ms. kvcache hit-rate on v2.8.0 is 72% vs 89% on v2.7.4 for the same workload.

josh: kvcache drop suggests a change in keying or cache warming behavior from the scheduler/quant path. check KV serialization or new prefix hashing.

sasha: good catch. grep recent commits around kvkey/serializer in runtime repo.

maria: found commit 9f3b2a: "change kv key to include quant tier" — that would definitely reduce cache reuse across requests.

roland: that explains p95 tail — more misses => slower long prompts. mitigation options:
- revert kv key change quickly for all traffic (fast, but invasive)
- patch runtime to fallback to old keying when a tenant flag set (safer, deploy rollout)
- increase cache capacity temporarily to mask misses (operational blunt instrument)

josh: short-term: set routing rule to send ACME to v2.7.4 until patch. medium-term: deploy hotfix that uses dual-key lookup (check new key then old key) for 24h to warm caches.

sasha: can we implement dual-key lookup in a small patch and roll to canary? code sketch:
```
// pseudo
val = kv_get(new_key);
if (!val) val = kv_get(old_key);
if (val) serve_from_cache(val);
else compute_and_insert(new_key);
```

eva: I'll build and smoke test that on a canary host. patch target branch: hotfix/kv-dual-lookup.

maria: meanwhile support update to customer: "we've identified a cache key change that reduces reuse; routing ACME to previous runtime for immediate relief and building a hotfix. Will update in 1h." :thumbsup:

support-bot: Customer notified for ticket #87912.

(2h later)

eva: canary hotfix deployed, dual-lookup enabled on 10% hosts. preliminary p95 on those hosts dropped ~15%.

josh: nice. start ramp to 50% and monitor p95/p99 and kv hit-rate.

maria: ramped to 50% at 2:15. metrics: cohort with hotfix p95=470ms, control v2.8.0=600ms. kv hit-rate improved to 84% on hotfix hosts.

roland: plan for full rollout after 2h of stable metrics. also prepare a postmortem item to add configuration gating for KV key schema changes and require a performance eval on tail percentiles before merge.

sasha: add an automated canary test that runs a synthetic seq-length sweep and validates p95 delta < 10% vs baseline. gate on PRs touching kv keying code.

maria: agreed. I'll open the RFC PR for the gating and add eval harness tests.

josh: final note — double-check billing impacts: if latency increases cause retries, we might see cost bump for ACME. support, please confirm billing usage and whether we should credit them for the degradation window.

support-bot: Billing review in progress for ticket #87912. Will propose a goodwill credit if we exceed SLA.

maria: thanks team. summary: root cause = kv key change coupled with quant/scheduler rollout; mitigation = route customer back to v2.7.4 + hotfix dual-lookup + gradual ramp; follow-ups = canary perf test, gating, postmortem and billing review.

josh: great work. reassigning follow-ups: eva -> hotfix rollout logs, sasha -> CI gate PR, roland -> postmortem doc, maria -> customer comms.

(reacts) sasha: :eyes:
maria: :rocket:
